table.name: alignment
table.purpose: Lookup table of superhero moral alignments (Good, Bad, Neutral, N/A), referenced by the superhero table to classify each hero's alignment.

col_001.name: alignment_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the alignment lookup table; surrogate integer identifier referenced by superhero rows (superhero.col_004 and superhero.col_010) to indicate the hero's alignment.

col_002.name: alignment_name
col_002.description: Human-readable alignment label: Good, Bad, Neutral, or N/A (unknown/not applicable).

table.name: attribute
table.purpose: Lookup table of hero attributes (e.g. Intelligence, Speed, Durability, Combat, Power) referenced by hero_attribute.

col_001.name: attribute_id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate identifier for each attribute, referenced by hero_attribute.

col_002.name: attribute_name
col_002.description: Name of the hero attribute (Intelligence, Speed, Durability, Combat, Power, and one more unseen value).

table.name: colour
table.purpose: Lookup table of colours (35 rows), referenced by the superhero table for eye, hair, and skin colour attributes.

col_001.name: colour_id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate identifier for each colour. Referenced by superhero columns for eye, hair, and skin colour.

col_002.name: colour_name
col_002.description: Unique name of the colour (e.g. Black, Magenta, Pink, Strawberry Blond, Silver).

table.name: gender
table.purpose: Lookup table of genders for superheroes; referenced by the superhero table (two foreign key columns).

col_001.name: gender_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the gender lookup table; surrogate integer id (1-3) referenced by superhero columns col_004 and col_010.

table.name: hero_attribute
table.purpose: Junction table linking each superhero to one of six attributes (Intelligence, Strength, Speed, Durability, Power, Combat) with a numeric rating from 5 to 100. Each row is one superhero's score on one attribute; 623 heroes x 6 attributes = 3738 rows.

col_001.name: hero_id
col_001.description: Reference to superhero.col_001, the superhero this rating belongs to. Each hero appears 6 times (once per attribute).

col_002.name: attribute_id
col_002.description: Reference to attribute.col_001, the attribute being rated: 1=Intelligence, 2=Strength (implied, missing from lookup sample), 3=Speed, 4=Durability, 5=Power, 6=Combat.

col_003.name: value
col_003.description: The hero's rating for the attribute, on a 5-100 scale (integer, mean ~52). The join to superpower.col_001 is likely spurious/coincidental given the value range; the column is a rating score, not a superpower reference.

table.name: hero_power
table.purpose: Junction/association table linking superheroes to their superpowers (many-to-many between superhero and superpower). Each row records that a given hero has a given power.

col_001.name: hero_id
col_001.description: Identifier of the superhero; references superhero.col_001. Many rows per hero (a hero has multiple powers).

col_002.name: power_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the superpower; references superpower.col_001. Many rows per power (a power is shared by many heroes).

table.name: publisher
table.purpose: Lookup table of publishers/creators of superhero characters (comic studios, media companies, individual authors). Each row is one publisher, referenced by superhero.col_009.

col_001.name: publisher_id
col_001.description: Primary key, surrogate integer identifier for the publisher. Referenced by superhero.col_009 (many superheroes to one publisher).

col_002.name: publisher_name
col_002.description: Name of the publisher/creator (e.g. 'DC Comics', 'Shueisha', 'J. K. Rowling'). Unique across rows; one row has an empty string (unknown/unspecified publisher).

table.name: race
table.purpose: Lookup table of superhero races/species (e.g. Human, Alien, Mutant, Android), referenced by the superhero table to classify each character's race.

col_001.name: race_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique integer identifier for each race. Referenced by foreign keys in the superhero table.

col_002.name: race_name
col_002.description: Name of the race or species (e.g. Human / Radiation, Inhuman, Mutant, Vampire, Android). Unique per row; '-' likely denotes unknown/none.

table.name: superhero
table.purpose: One row per superhero/character, with core attributes (identity, alignment, gender, physical appearance, race, publisher, height, weight) linked to lookup tables; powers and attributes are attached via hero_power and hero_attribute junction tables.

col_001.name: superhero_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique integer identifier for each superhero row (1-756). Referenced by hero_power and hero_attribute.

col_002.name: superhero_name
col_002.description: The character's superhero/alias name (e.g. 'Green Lantern V', 'Iceman', 'King Kong'). Nearly unique; a few names shared by multiple characters.

col_003.name: full_name
col_003.description: The character's real/secret identity full name (e.g. 'Jessica Viviana Cruz', 'Barbara Gordon'). '-' or null when unknown.

col_004.name: alignment_id
col_004.description: Foreign key to alignment lookup (1=Good, 2=Bad, 3=Neutral). Distribution 519/203/28 matches a mostly-good roster. Could alternatively be gender (1=Male, 2=Female, 3=N/A), but col_010 is the more likely gender column; see col_010.

col_005.name: eye_colour_id
col_005.description: Foreign key to colour lookup; most likely eye colour (21 distinct values, top values 7, 1, 9, 14, 23). Could be hair colour instead - the order of the three colour columns (col_005/006/007) is not certain.

col_006.name: hair_colour_id
col_006.description: Foreign key to colour lookup; most likely hair colour (26 distinct values, more varied than col_005). Could be eye colour instead - order of the three colour columns is not certain.

col_007.name: skin_colour_id
col_007.description: Foreign key to colour lookup; most likely skin colour, since 681/750 rows share one value (1, presumably a default like 'human skin tone' or the first colour). Could be another appearance colour, but the heavy concentration on a single value fits skin colour best.

col_008.name: race_id
col_008.description: Foreign key to race lookup (61 distinct races; top values 1 and 24, likely 'Human' and a common non-human race such as 'Mutant').

col_009.name: publisher_id
col_009.description: Foreign key to publisher lookup (13=Marvel Comics with 387 rows, 4=DC Comics with 224 rows, 1 likely another large publisher).

col_010.name: gender_id
col_010.description: Foreign key to gender lookup (1=Male, 2=Female, 3=N/A); distribution 504/212/28 fits a male-dominated roster. Could alternatively be alignment (1=Good, 2=Bad, 3=Neutral), but col_004 is the more likely alignment column.

col_011.name: height_cm
col_011.description: Character height in centimetres. 0 or null means unknown; typical values cluster 159-188 cm. Outliers like 10800 and max 30480 are data errors or non-human characters (e.g. giant creatures).

col_012.name: weight_kg
col_012.description: Character weight in kilograms. 0 or null means unknown; typical values cluster 3.5-98 kg. Extreme max 90,000,000 is a data error or non-human character.

table.name: superpower
table.purpose: Lookup table of superpowers/superhero abilities; one row per distinct power, referenced by hero_power and hero_attribute.

col_001.name: superpower_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique surrogate identifier for each superpower (1-167).

col_002.name: superpower_name
col_002.description: Unique human-readable name of the superpower (e.g. 'Accelerated Healing', 'Invisibility').
